annotations.text:
The hover tip on an upgrade hexagon — four registers for the same three facts.

Every card shows the same two cases so they are comparable: a four-deep weapon (delta, span, run ledger) and a capped stat card. Words in [DRAFT] are the tip's own chrome and are still Ethan's to write — see design/COPY-TODO.md. Every number is real: measured from apply(), or off the run ledger.

WHY — it is already there, already tested, and it is the only one of the four that survives a card moving four stats at once: the phrase can run to three lines and the table still holds.

COST — it is a dialog box. Nothing about it says this game rather than any settings panel, and at four rows it is the tallest of the four over a fight.

WHY — the run already prints things. The kill shots come out of a camera onto paper, and a tip on the same stock says the game keeps records rather than that a UI framework does.

COST — a bright rectangle over a dark fight is loud, and it reads as an OBJECT in the world when the corner hive it points at is a readout. Also the one direction that cannot be dimmed without looking grubby.

WHY — the span stops being two numbers and becomes a distance. It borrows the health and air gauges' own gradients, so it is legible at a glance and unmistakably from this HUD.

COST — a bar can only show ONE stat, so a card that moves four has to pick a lead and drop the rest, or grow four bars. It also needs a floor and a ceiling, and half the stats in the game have neither.

WHY — no chrome at all, so nothing covers the fight. Three lines of type that a player who knows the roster reads in under a second, and the only one of the four that could stay up mid-run.

COST — unlearnable. Nothing tells you what 261k · 92 is, so it is a reward for people who already know rather than an explanation for people who do not — which is the opposite of what the tip was built for.

MOBILE — whichever wins, the tip now opens on a HOLD (280ms, matching the pause button) on the level-up cards, the corner hive, the boss dividend and the end-of-run build. A hold cancels the pick, so reading a card is no longer the same gesture as taking it, and pulling your thumb off cancels both. Direction D is the only one small enough to hold under a thumb without the thumb covering it — worth a look on a phone before deciding.
